chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I asked him about: “The ʿawrah of the believer is forbidden to the believer.” He said: “Yes.” I said: “I mean his lower private parts.” He said: “It is not where you are going; rather, it means divulging his secret.”

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: The believer; a person of faith whose dignity and privacy are to be protected.
key_terms.سِرِّهِ: His secret; a matter entrusted to privacy.
key_terms.عَوْرَةُ: That which must be concealed; here, interpreted as a believer’s private and confidential matters.

ai.seo_question: What does “the ʿawrah of the believer is forbidden to the believer” mean in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the sanctity of a believer’s “ʿawrah” is not limited here to physical nakedness. Rather, its intended meaning is the prohibition of exposing and spreading a believer’s private secrets, highlighting the inviolability of trust and personal confidentiality among believers.
